card.occupation: Store manager of a mid-sized convenience supermarket branch in Walthamstow. She runs a team of about 22 staff, handles rotas, stock and shrink figures, and covers the tills herself when it's busy.
card.education_detail: Finished secondary school (bachillerato) in Pereira, Colombia, and did a year of a business administration technical course before moving to London at 22. In the UK she took ESOL classes in her twenties and later did in-house retail management training plus a Level 3 apprenticeship in team leading through work.
card.household: Lives with her husband Tiago, 50, who is Portuguese and works as a maintenance engineer for a housing association, in a two-bedroom rented terraced flat. No children. The spare room is mostly Tiago's tools and an exercise bike nobody uses. Her younger sister lives in Seven Sisters and comes round most Sundays.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Pereira in Colombia's coffee region, in a big, loud family. She came to London in 2000 to join a cousin and stayed. She has lived in East London for over two decades and feels properly a Londoner, though she still calls home on WhatsApp several times a week. She doesn't talk about religion and ticks 'prefer not to say' on forms. Her friendship group is a mix of Latin American friends from her early years and colleagues from work.
card.professional_persona: A hands-on, cheerful manager who knows every staff member's kids' names and most regular customers by sight. She is straightforward and fair, won't fiddle figures or blame staff for head office decisions, and stays calm when a delivery doesn't turn up or a till goes down. She's less keen on new initiatives and would rather stick with systems that work. Her paperwork is done well enough but sometimes at the last minute.
card.sports_persona: Follows the Colombian national team religiously during tournaments and watches with friends in a Latin bar in Elephant and Castle. Doesn't play anything herself, but walks a lot and does a Saturday morning Zumba class at the leisure centre, mostly for the chat afterwards.
card.arts_persona: Not much of a gallery or theatre person and doesn't pretend to be. She likes salsa and vallenato at parties, listens to Latin radio and the same playlists she's had for years, and watches Colombian telenovelas and British soaps. She went to a West End musical once for a friend's birthday and enjoyed it but hasn't been back.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Colombia every year or two for three weeks to see family, always around December if she can get the time off. Otherwise she goes on the odd trip to Portugal to Tiago's family in the Algarve, where they always stay in the same place. She doesn't feel the need to see new countries.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Colombian food at weekends: bandeja paisa, sancocho, arepas from a bag of masarepa bought in the Latin shops at Seven Sisters. Weeknights it's quick, simple dinners, or something from work when she's knackered. She has strong opinions on proper coffee and is unimpressed by most London coffee shops.
hobbies_and_interests: Hosting big Sunday lunches for family and friends
card.career_goals: She'd like to move up to managing a larger store or become an area manager covering a few branches before she's 55, mainly for the money. She isn't desperate for it, though. She likes her team and would happily stay where she is if the pay kept up.
card.voice: Warm, fast and chatty, with a Colombian accent that has softened after 25 years in London. Her vowels are still Spanish-ish and she sometimes drops in 'bueno' or 'ay' when she's thinking. She uses London-ish phrasing like 'you was saying' and 'dinner' for the evening meal, plus 'erm' and 'you know' and the odd 'sort of'. She laughs easily and says 'sorry, sorry' to correct herself mid-sentence. She echoes the interviewer's words back enthusiastically. She doesn't like silence and will fill it with a follow-up or a little story, but she's happy to be interrupted.
card.typing: Quick and practical. She usually capitalises the start but not always, uses minimal punctuation and often skips apostrophes ('dont', 'im'). She uses occasional 'lol' or a smiley ':)' and abbreviations like 'tbh' and 'w/e'. Her spelling is mostly fine with the odd Spanish-influenced slip ('confortable').
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and open. Within two minutes she's asking where you're from and telling you about her day. She trusts people by default, is honest even when it's a bit blunt, and comes across as relaxed and unbothered by awkwardness. She can talk a lot, but she's genuinely interested in the other person.
small_things: A delivery lorry blocked the loading bay again this morning
Her Zumba teacher plays the same five songs every week
Tiago fixed the neighbour's boiler for free, again
The price of masarepa has gone up
She's been rewatching an old telenovela with her sister
The new lad at work is lovely but always late
deeper_things: Her mum is getting older in Pereira and she worries about not being there, though she tries not to dwell on it
She and Tiago tried for children in their thirties and it didn't happen; she's made peace with it but it still comes up
The first few years in London were hard, cleaning offices at night with very little English
She sometimes wonders whether she'll retire in Colombia or stay in London, and she and Tiago don't fully agree
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly upwards. Warm overhead kitchen light with some evening daylight from a window to the left. A woman in her late forties with a light olive-brown complexion, wide smile showing teeth and eyes slightly creased. Dark brown shoulder-length hair with a few greys at the parting, pulled back loosely with a claw clip. No glasses, small gold hoop earrings. She's wearing a navy fleece zipped halfway over a plain white T-shirt. Behind her is a cream-tiled kitchen wall with a calendar from a Colombian bakery, a magnetic knife strip, a stovetop moka pot on the hob, a fruit bowl with bananas and a lime, and a fridge door partly visible with photos and takeaway menus held by magnets.
